findings.title: All twelve success criteria trace to tasks; sequencing, granularity, and proportionality check out
findings.description:
Cross-referencing each success criterion in the slice design against the breakdown:

- **SC1 (flow selection)** → Task 1.1/1.2; live behavior verified in 8.5, as the task itself defers to.
- **SC2 (only two fixed questions + one confirmation, extraction first)** → Tasks 5.1 (verbatim text, once-as-one-block timing), 5.2 (three confirmation outcomes), 5.3 (byte-identical diff, interaction inventory), and 8.1's "nothing else asked" check.
- **SC3 (citation/attribution rules; signals as observations)** → Tasks 3.1–3.3 author the three source disciplines; 3.4 executes them against this repo; 8.1 confirms `README.md` citations in the output.
- **SC4 (dropped topics nowhere)** → Task 4.1's dropped-topics rule plus 4.2's row-for-row diff, including the "Target Users … never asked" check.
- **SC5 (decline → gap marker + provenance, no prose fill)** → Task 5.1's decline semantics; exercised in 8.2 on a scratch tree.
- **SC6 (verbatim answers, preservation, dated subheading)** → Task 6.1 write rules; re-run behavior in 6.2; verified in 8.4 (`git diff` byte-identity).
- **SC7 (loud terminal stop on guide failure)** → Tasks 2.1 (preconditions 2–3 with terminal stops) and 6.1 (both checks with distinct stop messages); exercised in 8.3 against a scratch guide copy, never the real one.
- **SC8 (never overwrite; augment-or-stop; default stop; refillability)** → Task 6.2; verified in 8.4.
- **SC9 (frontmatter, filename from cf registration, divergence stated)** → Task 7.2; verified in 8.1 including `cf validate frontmatter` and the `squadron`/`squadron-ai` divergence.
- **SC10 (provenance outcome set, engagement/inferred lines, `[INFERRED]` rule)** → Tasks 7.1 and 7.3; verified in 8.1.
- **SC11 (graph discipline; only changed non-document file)** → Task 3.1's read-discipline statement; mechanically verified in 8.6 (`git status` on `.understand-anything/`, `git diff --stat main -- src/` empty).
- **SC12 (PM-would-edit concept)** → Task 8.1, live with the PM per the framing notice.

Every design Implementation Note also has a home: sibling-section placement (1.1), fixed question text (5.1), the Gap-markers pointer update (7.1), and the 362 cross-reference sentence fix (7.4). All design line references in the tasks are accurate — I confirmed the anchors in the actual skill file (`Flow: Comprehension Analysis` at `commands/analysis/understand.md:387`, the "slices 363 and 364" sentence in the flow's argument-handling paragraph, and the human-documentation divider at lines 631–633 that bounds the insertion point) and the slice-design line cites (verified-facts table at 110–121, flow-selection bullets at 137–148, signals checklist at 158–164, mapping table at 175–183, question text at 204–210, `[INFERRED]` rule at 277–280, frontmatter block at 299–312, walkthrough step 1 at 382–392, Implementation Notes at 441–448).

Sequencing is linear with no circularity; the one real dependency inside the walkthrough (8.4 re-running against the 8.1 document) is explicitly ordered after 8.1. Each authoring substep is immediately followed by a verification substep (1.2, 2.2, 3.4, 4.2, 5.3, 6.3, 8.x), which is the correct test-with pattern for a no-code slice. No task is oversized — 8.1's checklist is long but is a single live PM session enumerating design step 3's checks — and none is needlessly granular. Proportionality is right for a 3/5 slice: one task per design decision, one walkthrough task per design walkthrough step (1–7), plus branch/close hygiene. Task 8.6's `ruff`/`pytest` checks go slightly beyond the design's step 7 but are justified by the project's build-verification rule and the pack-install path this file ships in — cleared, not creep. The slice restates no NFR, so no load-test or CI-wiring task is owed. Commit markers sit at verified working points (after each authoring task's verification), not after every subtask and not only at the end; holding the generated concept uncommitted until 8.6 is explicit in the marker's own text ("include any fixes found during 8.x"), so no gap.

findings.title: Commit markers are checkbox subitems rather than the plain `**Commit**:` lines sibling task files use
findings.description: The eight commit markers in this file are formatted as checklist subitems (`- [ ] Commit: \`feat: ...\`` at lines 99, 125, 164, 185, 221, 254, 296, 351), whereas sibling task files (e.g. `144-tasks`, `145-tasks`, `147-tasks`, `128-tasks`) render the marker as a bold plain line (`**Commit**: \`...\``) outside the checklist. Placement and semantics are correct here — each marker sits after its task's verification step — and the checkbox form is arguably what this project's own CLAUDE.md checklist convention produces for task files, so this is informational only. Note that as checkbox items they invite being checked off by task-checker rather than standing out as commit instructions; if cross-slice consistency matters, converting them to the plain `**Commit**:` form is a one-line-each change, but nothing in the slice's success criteria requires it.
